what_happened: The email-check job was held because free disk was too low: 9.7 GB free against 10 GB needed. The job's own 16 GB writer build was kept until the checks pass, and the cleanup cannot reclaim a held job's own build. The person running Athena deleted that build folder by hand so the job could resume. The same gap came up earlier the same day, when a held job's 8.1 GB folder had to be deleted by hand.
cause: Disk use is not tracked as a budget. Athena keeps the build folders of held jobs, including a held job's own writer build, and its cleanup skips them. Nothing compares free disk with what the kept folders and the next stage need. Only a person can free the space, and the shortfall is found only when free space is nearly gone.
prevention: Make disk a managed budget. Before a job is held, or when free disk drops below the need, Athena reclaims what it can on its own. That means pruning the build folders of held jobs and the job's own writer build once a recoverable form exists, such as the committed diff or a patch saved in the job's state. If the build must stay, the job resumes by rebuilding from that saved diff. Athena also checks free disk against the kept folders plus the next stage's need before it admits or resumes a job. When space is still short, it reports exactly which folders can be removed and by how much, instead of ending the job as failed with an environment message.
proposed_request: Make Athena manage disk itself so a held job never needs a hand delete. (1) Before a job is held, save its writer output as a patch in the job's state directory. Then let the cleanup reclaim the held job's build folder, including its own writer build, whenever free disk is below the space the next stage needs. (2) A job that resumes after cleanup rebuilds from the saved patch, and the result must match the original build. (3) When a job is held for low disk, the hold message lists the reclaimable folders and their sizes. (4) Before a job is admitted or resumed, Athena compares free disk with the kept folders plus the stage's expected build size. Acceptance: a test with a held job whose build is larger than the free-disk shortfall shows the cleanup reclaims it and the job resumes without a hand delete. A second test shows the job resumes from the patch and passes its checks. A third test shows the hold message lists the folders and sizes.
